claims.statement: Verified fact: the European Commission's PVGIS provides free solar-radiation and photovoltaic-performance data with APIs for automated access.
Verified fact: EIOPA describes parametric insurance as paying on an objective predefined event or index rather than indemnifying the measured pure loss, which creates possible basis risk.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): a licensed carrier will pay a specialist administrator for small-commercial PV yield cover rather than build the telemetry, index, and claim rail internally.

contrary_evidence: PVGIS data and APIs are free and broadly accessible, so weather/yield modeling alone is readily copyable: https://joint-research-centre.ec.europa.eu/photovoltaic-geographical-information-system-pvgis_en

EIOPA's definition highlights that index payouts can diverge from actual loss; basis risk may make the product unattractive or harmful without careful calibration: https://www.eiopa.europa.eu/document/download/d8c87070-f602-4bf7-b8d8-726ec0b5c173_en

economics.acquisition_route: First sell a non-insurance yield-assurance dashboard to an O&M portfolio, then seek a licensed carrier to design a compliant cover using observed data.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 1,000 assets at PLN 400/year in year 2, 6,000 at PLN 500/year in year 4, and 15,000 at PLN 550/year in year 7 imply PLN 8.25m recurring revenue before claim fees. At 20% owner earnings or a 3-4x insurance-infrastructure value and 55% ownership, PLN 5m net worth is plausible in years 6-8; no licensed carrier interest after a validated 500-asset O&M dataset ends the risk-transfer thesis.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day for one inverter family and O&M portfolio; regulated product design, distribution, and underwriting remain with licensed partners.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 70-85% at sufficient portfolio density; telemetry normalization, data gaps, and claim review are variable costs.
economics.payback: Unvalidated payer hypothesis: automated monitoring and objective claim packets lower administration and enable a sellable cover; must be established with an insurer, not inferred from PV data availability.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 250-900 per monitored asset per year plus PLN 150-600 per calculated claim and paid portfolio integration; insurer sets premium and bears risk.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Assets are monitored for multi-year contracts, and calibrated configuration/telemetry histories improve each renewal.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: permissioned asset-level expected-versus-actual histories improve calibration, pricing support, and equipment/O&M segmentation while carrier integrations create switching costs
fingerprint.customer: licensed EU insurers or MGAs partnering with commercial rooftop installers and O&M portfolios of small-to-mid-sized PV assets
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: one licensed insurer/MGA design partner reached through solar O&M, installer, or insurance-broker channels; family company can supply non-policy workflow observations only
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: policy-configuration snapshot, telemetry and PVGIS ingestion, exclusion/event ledger, transparent index calculation, payout packet, and portfolio performance API
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: licensed carrier, MGA, or O&M program pays per asset-year monitored and per claim packet calculated; no founder risk capital is placed behind claims
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a monitored period closes below the contractual weather-adjusted yield trigger and a payout determination is due

founder_fit: Time-series modeling and uncertainty quantification fit the founder's data-science strengths.
The parents' renewables context aids product understanding and potential non-insurance telemetry pilots.
The structure avoids using the founder's limited capital to underwrite claims.
Partner and portfolio distribution avoids personal-brand media and can compound into a data asset.
risks: Selling or administering insurance without appropriate permissions would be unlawful; roles must be defined by counsel and licensed partners.
Basis risk can produce payouts that diverge from actual customer loss.
Inverter telemetry can be missing, altered, or vendor-restricted.
A carrier may copy the index or use an established catastrophe-modeling vendor.

structure.commercial_archetype: parametric risk-transfer data and claims administrator
structure.control_point: pre-agreed loss-index calculation that determines whether a covered solar-yield event triggers a contractual payout
structure.critical_dependency: licensed risk carrier plus reliable inverter telemetry, frozen system configuration, independent irradiance data, and an index with acceptable basis risk

thesis: Provide licensed insurers, MGAs, O&M firms, and commercial rooftop installers the data and administration layer for a narrowly defined solar-yield cover. At policy inception it freezes system configuration and an objective weather/yield index; during the term it ingests inverter telemetry and independent irradiance data; at trigger it calculates the contractual payout and produces a traceable claim packet. The company does not underwrite, distribute, or promise insurance without a licensed partner. The insurer pays per monitored asset-year and completed claim.
title: Parametric Solar-Yield Cover Administration Rail
uncertainties: No carrier demand, premium economics, or policyholder willingness has been validated.
The right trigger, exclusions, and minimum portfolio size are unknown.
PVGIS is suitable as an independent analytical input but not proven as a contractual oracle.
Data rights across installer, owner, O&M provider, inverter vendor, and insurer need validation.
